method: blinded A/B judgement by two independent fresh agents, one per description. Each was given the skill's name and one description and nothing else - no SKILL.md body, no repository - and asked, for each of the twenty queries, whether that entry alone would make it open the skill. This substitutes for skill-creator's scripts/run_eval.py, which is not trustworthy on this machine: see harness_note.
harness_note: skill-creator's scripts/run_eval.py runs, but its positive control fails here. It writes a slash-command file, runs `claude -p`, and counts a trigger only if the FIRST tool call is a Skill or Read naming that command; anything else is read as 'did not trigger'. This machine has a SessionStart hook that injects the superpowers doctrine into every nested session, so the nested agent opens a superpowers skill first and every query scores 0. Measured: the query 'Use the deckwright skill to build a five-slide deck ... output pptx' - which cannot be a false negative about a description - scored 0/1. Numbers from that harness would have been noise, so they are not reported.

before.description: Idea -> binding spec -> HTML draft -> native, editable PPTX, integrated into a deck a human keeps editing by hand, with a QA loop that proves the file opens and says what the spec said. Use when building consulting slides natively with python-pptx, retexting an approved deck without breaking its formatting, transplanting generated slides into someone else's file, or checking a deck before it goes to a client.

missed.query_summary: five slides off the user's own design system, no .pptx wanted, print to PDF
missed.judge_reason: no pptx needed, just HTML/PDF slides for screen

missed.query_summary: 'ok i need to make some slides for monday. nothing fancy'
missed.judge_reason: vague slide request, no pptx or QA need

missed.query_summary: adopt a client brand kit (tokens/ CSS, TTFs, wordmark) as the house style
missed.judge_reason: generic brand kit setup, no deck/slide mentioned

after.description: Turn an idea into a slide deck: a binding spec, HTML drafts drawn on a design system, then a native, editable PowerPoint file - or ship the HTML deck itself and print it to PDF - with a QA loop that proves the deliverable says what the spec said. Use this skill whenever someone wants a deck, slides, a presentation, a PPTX or an HTML deck built, rebuilt, restyled or checked: building slides on a company or client design system or brand, drafting a slide in HTML before any Python, retexting an approved deck without breaking its formatting, transplanting generated slides into a file a human keeps editing by hand, adding speaker notes or a teleprompter, diagnosing a deck PowerPoint wants to repair, or running lint, visual and file-integrity QA before it goes to a client. Use it even when the request is only "make me some slides" and names no tool or format. Not for merely reading a deck somebody sent: summarising or extracting from a .pptx needs no skill.

reading: The three the old description missed are the three things it never said: that the HTML deck is a deliverable in its own right (2026-09-10 ruling), that a bare 'make me some slides' is in scope, and that adopting somebody's design system as a brand package is a route this skill owns. None of the ten near-miss negatives moved - the added recall cost no precision, and query 11 (summarise a deck someone sent) was refused by the new description citing its own exclusion clause.
caveat: Two judges, one sample each, no repeats. This measures whether the description SAYS the thing, not the variance of a real router. Treat 17 -> 20 as a directional result, not a benchmark.
